number-depth: 2
format: 
    html:
        code-fold: false

```{=html}
<p>This example is based on the LIS (library) dataset. The library records every time a copy of a book is issued in one wide table, <b>issue_record</b>, whose columns are renamed <b>A, B, C, D, E, G</b>:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Letter</th><th>Column</th><th>Meaning</th><th>Example</th></tr><tr><td>A</td><td>member_no</td><td>library member</td><td>M0045</td></tr><tr><td>B</td><td>member_name</td><td>member’s name</td><td>Surendra Malik</td></tr><tr><td>C</td><td>accession_no</td><td>one physical copy of a book</td><td>9789386551337B</td></tr><tr><td>D</td><td>isbn</td><td>the book (edition)</td><td>9789386551337</td></tr><tr><td>E</td><td>title</td><td>book title</td><td>Coding For Beginners In Easy Steps</td></tr><tr><td>G</td><td>date_of_issue</td><td>day the copy was issued</td><td>2021-07-02</td></tr></table></div>
<p>We skip the letter F because <b>F</b> is used for the set of functional dependencies (F⁺, F<sub>c</sub>).</p>
```

## Setting Up the Table

```{=html}
<p>The table holds six real issues taken from the LIS dataset (<b>book_issue</b> joined with <b>members</b>, <b>book_copies</b> and <b>book_catalogue</b>), plus one history row (copy …337B issued again). The datasets are read-only, so the table is built in the <b>workspace</b>. Run this block first; every later query on this page uses it. Running it again simply rebuilds the table.</p>

```

```{.sql db="test_db"}
drop table if exists issue_record;

create table issue_record (
    a varchar(10),   -- member_no
    b varchar(50),   -- member_name
    c varchar(20),   -- accession_no
    d varchar(20),   -- isbn
    e varchar(100),  -- title
    g date           -- date_of_issue
);

insert into issue_record values
('M0060', 'Sanchita saha',  '9789386551337B', '9789386551337', 'Coding For Beginners In Easy Steps',  '2021-07-01'),
('M0045', 'Surendra Malik', '9789386551337C', '9789386551337', 'Coding For Beginners In Easy Steps',  '2021-07-02'),
('M0020', 'Suresh Singh',   '9789386551337A', '9789386551337', 'Coding For Beginners In Easy Steps',  '2021-07-03'),
('M0048', 'Rahul Singh',    '9789332543553B', '9789332543553', 'Programming in C',                    '2021-08-01'),
('M0045', 'Surendra Malik', '9789332543553C', '9789332543553', 'Programming in C',                    '2021-08-01'),
('M0001', 'Vikas Das',      '9789351199380A', '9789351199380', 'Advanced Database Management System', '2021-08-01'),
-- the added history row: copy ...337B issued again
('M0020', 'Suresh Singh',   '9789386551337B', '9789386551337', 'Coding For Beginners In Easy Steps',  '2021-08-05');

select * from issue_record order by g, c;
```

```{=html}

<p><b>The functional dependencies</b> the library states:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>FD</th><th>With attribute names</th></tr><tr><td>A → B</td><td>member_no → member_name</td></tr><tr><td>AG → B</td><td>member_no, date_of_issue → member_name</td></tr><tr><td>C → DE</td><td>accession_no → isbn, title</td></tr><tr><td>D → E</td><td>isbn → title</td></tr><tr><td>CG → AB</td><td>accession_no, date_of_issue → member_no, member_name</td></tr></table></div>
<p><b>F = { A → B, AG → B, C → DE, D → E, CG → AB }</b>. F is deliberately not minimal: some of these FDs are redundant and will be removed when we compute the canonical cover.</p>
```

## 1. Redundancy and Anomalies

```{=html}
<p>A good design stores each fact <b>once</b>. A fact is repeated when a table contains an FD whose left side is <b>not a key</b>: every row sharing that left side must repeat the right side.</p>
<div class="flow-label">How</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>find an FD</b></div><span>α → β in F</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>is α a key?</b></div><span>no: only CG is a key</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>count rows</b></div><span>sharing the same α</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>each row</b></div><span>repeats β</span></div></div>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>FD with a non-key left side</th><th>Fact stored</th><th>Times stored here</th></tr><tr><td>D → E<br><small>isbn → title</small></td><td>“9789386551337 is <i>Coding For Beginners In Easy Steps</i>”</td><td>4 (once per issue of that book)</td></tr><tr><td>A → B<br><small>member_no → member_name</small></td><td>“M0045 is Surendra Malik”</td><td>2</td></tr><tr><td>A → B<br><small>member_no → member_name</small></td><td>“M0020 is Suresh Singh”</td><td>2</td></tr></table></div>
<div class="panel"><h4>The three anomalies on this table</h4><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Anomaly</th><th>What happens in issue_record</th><th>Root cause</th></tr><tr><td><b>Update</b></td><td>Correct the title of 9789386551337 in one row only → the same isbn now has two titles.</td><td>D → E is stored 4 times</td></tr><tr><td><b>Insertion</b></td><td>A new book arrives but nobody has borrowed it. Its isbn and title cannot be stored: every row needs a copy (C) and an issue date (G), which are part of the key.</td><td>book facts are tied to issue facts</td></tr><tr><td><b>Deletion</b></td><td>Delete M0060’s only issue → the fact “M0060 is Sanchita saha” disappears from the database.</td><td>member facts are tied to issue facts</td></tr></table></div></div>
```

## 2. Atomic Domains and 1NF

```{=html}
<p>A domain is <b>atomic</b> if its values are treated as indivisible. A relation is in <b>first normal form (1NF)</b> if every attribute has an atomic domain. Look at column <b>C (accession_no)</b>:</p>
<div class="panel"><h4>C = 9789386551337B</h4><div class="flow"><div class="box"><b>9789386551337</b><span>the isbn (D) hidden inside C</span></div><div class="box grey"><b>B</b><span>the copy letter</span></div></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0">The accession number is the isbn followed by a copy letter: one value made of two parts.</p></div>
<p>Every column of issue_record holds one value per row, so the table is in <b>1NF</b> as long as C is used only as an identifier. In the LIS dataset, book_copies keeps isbn_no as its own column for exactly this reason.</p>
```

## 3. A Lossy Decomposition

```{=html}
<p>To remove redundancy we split a table into smaller tables. Splitting on the wrong column loses information. Try R₁ = (A, B, G) and R₂ = (G, C, D, E): the only common column is <b>G (date)</b>.</p>
<div class="flow-label">How</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>project</b></div><span>keep R₁’s and R₂’s columns</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>join</b></div><span>on the common column G</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>compare</b></div><span>with the original 7 rows</span></div></div>

```

```{.sql db="test_db"}
select count(*)
from (select distinct a, b, g from issue_record) as r1
     join (select distinct g, c, d, e from issue_record) as r2
     using (g);
```

```{=html}

<p>7 rows go in, <b>13</b> come out.</p>
<div class="panel"><h4>Where the 6 extra rows come from: 2021-08-01</h4><p style="margin:0 0 8px">3 members × 3 copies on 2021-08-01 = 9 rows, of which only 3 are real. Some of the fake rows:</p><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>A</th><th>B</th><th>C</th><th>E</th></tr><tr><td>M0001</td><td>Vikas Das</td><td>9789332543553B</td><td>Programming in C</td></tr><tr><td>M0045</td><td>Surendra Malik</td><td>9789351199380A</td><td>Advanced Database Management System</td></tr><tr><td>M0048</td><td>Rahul Singh</td><td>9789332543553C</td><td>Programming in C</td></tr><tr><td>…</td><td></td><td></td><td></td></tr></table></div></div>
<p>More rows is <b>less</b> information: we can no longer tell which of the 13 rows are real. G is not a key of either part, so the split is <b>lossy</b>. The lossless-join test shown later avoids this.</p>
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Lossless Join Check (split on date)" collapse="true"}

Click **Run** to see why splitting on G (date_of_issue) alone is lossy: G is not a key of either part.

```{.fd check="lossless-join"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB

Decompose: R1(A, B, G), R2(C, D, E, G)
```
:::

## 4. Functional Dependencies

```{=html}
<p>α → β holds if any two rows that agree on α also agree on β. To check an FD on a table:</p>
<div class="flow-label">How</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>group</b></div><span>rows by α</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>count</b></div><span>distinct β in each group</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>more than 1</b></div><span>that group violates α → β</span></div></div>

```

```{.sql db="test_db"}
-- does A → B hold on these rows?  (no output = no violation)
select a from issue_record
group by a having count(distinct b) > 1;

-- does C → A hold?
select c, count(distinct a) from issue_record
group by c having count(distinct a) > 1;
```

```{=html}

<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Check on the 7 rows</th><th>Result</th><th>Why</th></tr><tr><td>A → B<br><small>member_no → member_name</small></td><td>✓ satisfied</td><td>M0045 and M0020 each appear twice, always with the same name</td></tr><tr><td>D → E<br><small>isbn → title</small></td><td>✓ satisfied</td><td>each isbn always has the same title</td></tr><tr><td>C → A<br><small>accession_no → member_no</small> ?</td><td>✗ violated</td><td>copy …337B: M0060 on 07-01, M0020 on 08-05</td></tr><tr><td>A → C<br><small>member_no → accession_no</small> ?</td><td>✗ violated</td><td>M0045 has two different copies</td></tr><tr><td>G → A<br><small>date_of_issue → member_no</small> ?</td><td>✗ violated</td><td>three members on 2021-08-01</td></tr></table></div>
<p><b>Trivial FD:</b> α → β is trivial if β ⊆ α. Example: <b>CG → C</b> (accession_no, date_of_issue → accession_no) always holds, in every table, so it says nothing about the library.</p>
```

## 5. Armstrong’s Axioms

```{=html}
<p>Armstrong’s axioms derive the FDs that follow from F; they are <b>sound</b> and <b>complete</b>.</p>
<p>Derive <b>CG → E</b>, i.e. accession_no, date_of_issue → title (“a copy on a date determines the title”):</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Step</th><th>FD</th><th>Reason</th></tr><tr><td>1</td><td>CG → C</td><td>reflexivity (C ⊆ CG)</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td>C → DE</td><td>given</td></tr><tr><td>3</td><td>CG → DE</td><td>transitivity of 1 and 2</td></tr><tr><td>4</td><td>CG → E</td><td>decomposition of 3</td></tr></table></div>
```

## 6. Attribute Closure

```{=html}
<p>α⁺ = every attribute that α determines under F.</p>
<div class="flow-label">How</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>start</b></div><span>result = α</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>scan F</b></div><span>each FD β → γ</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>if β ⊆ result</b></div><span>add γ</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>repeat</b></div><span>until nothing changes</span></div></div>
<div class="panel"><h4>(CG)⁺ step by step</h4><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Step</th><th>FD used</th><th>result so far</th></tr><tr><td>start</td><td></td><td>C G</td></tr><tr><td>1</td><td>C → DE</td><td>C G D E</td></tr><tr><td>2</td><td>CG → AB</td><td>C G D E A B</td></tr><tr><td>3</td><td>A → B, D → E</td><td>no change: stop</td></tr></table></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0">(CG)⁺ = <b>ABCDEG</b>, every column.</p></div>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>α</th><th>α⁺</th><th>Meaning</th></tr><tr><td>C</td><td>CDE</td><td>a copy tells you its isbn and title, not who has it</td></tr><tr><td>A</td><td>AB</td><td>a member number tells you only the name</td></tr><tr><td>D</td><td>DE</td><td>an isbn tells you the title</td></tr><tr><td>G</td><td>G</td><td>a date alone tells you nothing</td></tr></table></div>
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Attribute Closure (α⁺)" collapse="true"}

Click **Run**, then toggle attributes in the pills bar to compute C⁺, A⁺, D⁺ and G⁺ from the table above.

```{.fd check="closure"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB

Query: CG
```
:::

## 7. Keys and Testing FDs with Closure

```{=html}
<p>K is a <b>superkey</b> if K⁺ = R, and a <b>candidate key</b> if no smaller subset is also a superkey.</p>
<div class="panel"><h4>Finding every candidate key</h4><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>1</b></div><span>C and G appear on no right side → every key must contain both</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>2</b></div><span>(CG)⁺ = ABCDEG → CG is a superkey</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>3</b></div><span>C⁺ and G⁺ are not all → CG is minimal</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>4</b></div><span>so CG is the only candidate key</span></div></div></div>
<p>An attribute that never appears on a right side can never be derived, so it must be in every key.</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Term</th><th>Here</th></tr><tr><td>candidate key</td><td>CG (accession_no, date_of_issue)</td></tr><tr><td>prime attributes</td><td>C, G</td></tr><tr><td>non-prime attributes</td><td>A, B, D, E</td></tr><tr><td>number of superkeys</td><td>every superset of CG: 2⁴ = 16</td></tr></table></div>
<p>In real terms: one issue is identified by <b>which copy</b> and <b>which day</b>.</p>
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Candidate Keys" collapse="true"}

Click **Run** to confirm that CG is the only candidate key, with C and G as the prime attributes.

```{.fd check="candidate-keys"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB
```
:::

## 8. Extraneous Attributes and Canonical Cover

```{=html}
<p>An attribute is <b>extraneous</b> if removing it does not change F⁺. The tests:</p>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Side</th><th>To test attribute X in α → β</th><th>X is extraneous if</th></tr><tr><td>left</td><td>compute (α − X)⁺ using F</td><td>β ⊆ (α − X)⁺</td></tr><tr><td>right</td><td>replace α → β by α → (β − X), then compute α⁺ with that set</td><td>X ∈ α⁺</td></tr></table></div>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>FD</th><th>Attribute</th><th>Test</th><th>Extraneous?</th></tr><tr><td>AG → B</td><td>G (left side)</td><td>A⁺ using F = AB. Contains B?</td><td>✓ yes, remove G → A → B</td></tr><tr><td>C → DE</td><td>E (right side)</td><td>use C → D instead; C⁺ = C, D, then D → E gives E</td><td>✓ yes, remove E → C → D</td></tr><tr><td>CG → AB</td><td>B (right side)</td><td>use CG → A instead; (CG)⁺ still gets B through A → B</td><td>✓ yes → CG → A</td></tr><tr><td>CG → A</td><td>C or G (left)</td><td>C⁺ = CDE, G⁺ = G: neither contains A</td><td>✗ keep both</td></tr></table></div>
<div class="panel"><h4>From F to F<sub>c</sub></h4><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>F</b></div><span>A → B, AG → B, C → DE, D → E, CG → AB</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>remove extraneous</b></div><span>A → B, A → B, C → D, D → E, CG → A</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>merge duplicates</b></div><span>F<sub>c</sub></span></div></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0;font-size:1.1rem"><b>F<sub>c</sub> = { A → B, C → D, D → E, CG → A }</b></p></div>
<p>F and F<sub>c</sub> are <b>equivalent</b>: each FD of one can be derived from the other.</p>
<p>F<sub>c</sub> says exactly what F says, with no redundant attribute. Each FD of F<sub>c</sub> describes one real thing: A → B a member, C → D a copy, D → E a book, CG → A an issue. That is the blueprint for the decomposition that follows. Note that C → DE was redundant because the title depends on the <b>isbn</b>, not directly on the copy.</p>
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Extraneous Attribute Check" collapse="true"}

Click **Run** to test each attribute of each FD in F, as in the table above.

```{.fd check="extraneous-attribute"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Canonical Cover (F_c)" collapse="true"}

Click **Run** to reduce F to F<sub>c</sub> = { A → B, C → D, D → E, CG → A } step by step.

```{.fd check="canonical-cover"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB
```
:::

## 9. A Lossless-Join Decomposition

```{=html}
<p>Splitting R into R₁, R₂ is <b>lossless</b> if the common columns are a key of at least one side: R₁ ∩ R₂ → R₁ or R₁ ∩ R₂ → R₂.</p>
<div class="flow-label">How</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>pick an FD</b></div><span>α → β from F<sub>c</sub></span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>split</b></div><span>(α ∪ β) and (R − β)</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>common part</b></div><span>is α, a key of the first table</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>repeat</b></div><span>on the remaining table</span></div></div>
<div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Split</th><th>Common</th><th>Why it is lossless</th></tr><tr><td>R → (A, B) + (A, C, D, E, G)</td><td>A (member_no)</td><td>A → B, so A is a key of (A, B)</td></tr><tr><td>(A, C, D, E, G) → (D, E) + (A, C, D, G)</td><td>D (isbn)</td><td>D → E, so D is a key of (D, E)</td></tr><tr><td>(A, C, D, G) → (C, D) + (A, C, G)</td><td>C (accession_no)</td><td>C → D, so C is a key of (C, D)</td></tr></table></div>
<div class="panel"><h4>The result: four tables, each about one thing</h4><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Schema</th><th>Real meaning</th><th>Key</th></tr><tr><td>(A, B)</td><td>member(member_no, member_name)</td><td>A</td></tr><tr><td>(C, D)</td><td>copy(accession_no, isbn)</td><td>C</td></tr><tr><td>(D, E)</td><td>book(isbn, title)</td><td>D</td></tr><tr><td>(A, C, G)</td><td>issue(member_no, accession_no, date)</td><td>CG</td></tr></table></div></div>
<p>Check it: join the four projections back together.</p>

```

```{.sql db="test_db"}
select count(*)
from (select distinct a, b from issue_record) as member
     join (select distinct c, g, a from issue_record) as issue using (a)
     join (select distinct c, d from issue_record) as copy using (c)
     join (select distinct d, e from issue_record) as book using (d);
```

```{=html}

<p>Exactly the 7 original rows come back (the lossy split on the date gave 13).</p>
<p>This is very close to the real LIS dataset, which has members, book_copies, book_catalogue and book_issue. Every anomaly found at the start is gone: a title is stored once, a new book can be added with no issue, and deleting an issue keeps the member.</p>
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Lossless Join Check (four tables)" collapse="true"}

Click **Run** to trace the lossless join of member, issue, copy and book step by step.

```{.fd check="lossless-join"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB

Decompose: R1(A, B), R2(C, D), R3(D, E), R4(A, C, G)
```
:::

## 10. Dependency Preservation

```{=html}
<p>A decomposition <b>preserves dependencies</b> if every FD can be checked <b>inside one table</b>, without joining.</p>
<div class="panel"><h4>The member / copy / book / issue decomposition</h4><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>FD of F<sub>c</sub></th><th>Checked in</th></tr><tr><td>A → B<br><small>member_no → member_name</small></td><td>member (A, B)</td></tr><tr><td>C → D<br><small>accession_no → isbn</small></td><td>copy (C, D)</td></tr><tr><td>D → E<br><small>isbn → title</small></td><td>book (D, E)</td></tr><tr><td>CG → A<br><small>accession_no, date_of_issue → member_no</small></td><td>issue (A, C, G)</td></tr></table></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0">Every FD lives in one table: <b>dependency preserving</b>.</p></div>
<p>Now a different split, also lossless: <b>(C, D), (C, E), (A, C, G), (A, B)</b>. Here the title is stored with the copy instead of with the book. Is D → E (isbn → title) preserved? Use the F′ method: collect the FDs that hold inside each table, then take closures under their union F′.</p>
<div class="flow-label">How</div><div class="flow steps"><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>local FDs</b></div><span>Fᵢ = FDs of F⁺ inside Rᵢ</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>combine</b></div><span>F′ = F₁ ∪ F₂ ∪ …</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>for each α → β in F</b></div><span>compute α⁺ under F′</span></div><div class="arrow">→</div><div class="step"><div class="box"><b>β ⊆ α⁺?</b></div><span>preserved, else lost</span></div></div>
<div class="panel"><h4>Is D → E preserved? The F′ method</h4><div class="table-wrap"><table class="jt res"><tr><th>Table</th><th>Local FDs</th></tr><tr><td>(C, D)</td><td>C → D</td></tr><tr><td>(C, E)</td><td>C → E (from C → D and D → E)</td></tr><tr><td>(A, C, G)</td><td>CG → A</td></tr><tr><td>(A, B)</td><td>A → B</td></tr></table></div><p style="margin:8px 0 0">F′ = { C → D, C → E, CG → A, A → B }. No FD in F′ has D alone on the left, so D⁺ under F′ = D, which does not contain E: <b>D → E is not preserved</b>. D and E never meet in one table.</p></div>
<p>In practice, one isbn could be stored with two different titles, and no single table could catch it.</p>
<p>A good decomposition is both <b>lossless</b> (no fake rows) and <b>dependency preserving</b> (every rule checkable in one table). The member / copy / book / issue design is both; the split that stores the title with the copy is lossless but not preserving.</p>
```

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Dependency Preservation Check (title with the book)" collapse="true"}

Click **Run** to see that every FD is preserved when the title is stored with the book.

```{.fd check="dependency-preservation"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB

Decompose: R1(A, B), R2(C, D), R3(D, E), R4(A, C, G)
```
:::

::: {.callout-tip title="Try it yourself: Dependency Preservation Check (title with the copy)" collapse="true"}

Click **Run** to see that D → E (isbn → title) is lost when the title is stored with the copy.

```{.fd check="dependency-preservation"}
R(A, B, C, D, E, G)

A -> B
AG -> B
C -> DE
D -> E
CG -> AB

Decompose: R1(C, D), R2(C, E), R3(A, C, G), R4(A, B)
```
:::
